items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Terminology 47:1
items.html: The Mochin of Katnut of ZON are called permanent Mochin, that is, that they never depart from it. So too all the Mochin that are from the discernment of Panim be'Achor of Nekudim — that is, even the Mochin of Gadlut in the Partzufim of Atik, AA, and AVI of Atzilut. However, the Mochin from the discernment of the MAN of the Yesod of AK that is in Nekudim, which are the Gadlut of ZA, and likewise the additions of Gadlut in the first three Partzufim, which come from the discernment of the MAN of the Vav and the point — all these are regarded as discernments of additions, and are not permanent in the Partzuf, but depart at the time of the blemish of the lower ones, as written at length (p. 657, in Inner Light, Sub Header, “Coupling,” see the whole continuation there). And there is a further sense in the word “permanent,” for the lights that belong to the substance of the Partzuf’s structure are also called permanent, as written above in Answer 15. (p. 647, Item 51)
